headline: Chiliz Governance Staking discovery blocked by restricted documentation access; PoSA system identified but contract addresses not enumerated
short_headline: Documentation access blocked; system identified but addresses unknown

findings.text: Chiliz Chain block explorer at scan.chiliz.com is live (Blockscout instance) but returned only metadata headers without searchable contract data or name-tag listings.

Chiliz docs reference 'Smart Contract Addresses' and 'Inflation Supply Allocation Addresses' pages (docs.chiliz.com) but full page content was not accessible; off-chain docs only outline governance structure (PoSA, 11 validators, ⅔ consensus) without listing deployment addresses.
No audit links provided in protocol metadata; no audit PDFs available to extract contract addresses.

GitHub repository chiliz-chain/v2 exists and documents PoSA consensus architecture and Parlia system contracts, but no deployment artifacts (broadcast JSONs, hardhat-deploy configs, or address indexes) were found in the repo structure to pin deployed contract addresses.
Protocol operates on single chain: Chiliz (chainId 88888). No multi-chain enumeration needed.
No factory contracts identified; protocol uses system contracts for validator set management, not enumerable child pools.

Role taxonomy applied but no addresses catalogued: Parlia consensus engine manages 'system contracts' for liveness slash, revenue distribution, and validator set renewal. Staking contract exists but address not retrieved.
No addresses passed ratchet threshold: Socios.com staking contract (0x5ff7f9724fd477d9a07dcdb894d0ca7f8fae1501) surfaces in search results but is for Fan Token staking, not CHZ governance staking.

rationale.verdict: Discovery assessment cannot proceed: Chiliz Governance Staking governance/control surface exists (PoSA validators, staking rewards, governance proposals) and is well-documented in off-chain sources, but the contract addresses on Chiliz Chain mainnet could not be enumerated from on-chain sources (explorer restrictions) or GitHub deployment artifacts. The staking contract is described as Parlia-compatible system contract but without a specific address to anchor further investigation. A successful discovery run requires either (a) direct access to scan.chiliz.com contract database or (b) deployment artifact JSON files in the GitHub repo.

evidence.shows: Official Chiliz governance staking portal confirmed; describes staking, reward earning, and validator delegation mechanism
Primary Chiliz Chain website describing staking as integral to PoSA consensus and governance participation; references governance portal and validator structure
Official Chiliz Chain v2 repository documents Parlia consensus engine and system contracts for liveness, slash, revenue distribution; no deployment artifacts accessible
Block explorer exists (Blockscout) but does not return searchable contract listings or name-tag data via web fetch
Staking documentation describes PoSA governance, validator roles, and reward distribution; references 'Smart Contract Addresses' page but full contract list not accessible
Main docs hub references 'Smart Contract Addresses' and 'Inflation Supply Allocation Addresses' but full page restricted

unknowns: D1-offchain: scan.chiliz.com block explorer did not return searchable contract listings or name-tag data; web fetch returned metadata headers only
D2-offchain: docs.chiliz.com Smart Contract Addresses page exists (referenced in content indexes) but full page content restricted from access
D4: chiliz-chain/v2 GitHub repository lacks deployment artifact JSONs (broadcast/, deployments/, addresses.json); cannot pin specific contract SHAs
D7: Parlia system contract role and governance contract addresses not enumerated; only architecture documented
D8: No confirmed CHZ governance staking contract address sourced; Socios.com Fan Token staking contract surfaces but is out-of-scope

protocol_metadata.about: Chiliz Chain is an EVM-compatible blockchain built for sports and entertainment brands, using Proof of Staked Authority (PoSA) consensus with 11 validators. Users stake CHZ tokens to validators to earn staking rewards and participate in on-chain governance through proposal voting, where ⅔ validator consensus is required for changes to pass.
